One should cause it to digest by means of that seed; through this sequential yoga, one attains penetration of a hundred thousand (*lakṣavedha*). By this process, the mercury becomes capable of penetration of ten million (*koṭivedhī*).
However, when the *vajra* alone has been fully digested, one should cause it to digest [the mercury].
Then the mercury (sūta) should be known as bound—unshakable and free from affliction.
Residing in the fire, the mercury arises; in an instant it swallows the rod.
Being smelted by the forceful fire, it eagerly swallows everything.
It moves and digests, O Sūta; it bestows longevity and wealth.
One should smelt the mercury situated in the crucible; it does not tremble at all in the fierce fire.
It digests all jewels; when bound, it leads to the power of moving through the sky (*khecaratā*).
Thus, when the metal has been multiplied eightfold and digested, there occurs the binding of mercury.

When the metals and the *sattva* have been tripled, and likewise the gold doubled, it becomes a penetrator (*vedhin*) by the sight of its fumes; such mercury shall be the bestower of liberation (*nirvāṇada*).

First, one should digest the eightfold [substances]: the essence of space (*vyomasattva*), the great elixir (*mahārasa*), and [other ingredients] equal to one-tenth part of the gold; one should digest the diamond-jewels (*vajraratna*). One should digest all these as diamonds (*vajra*); then this mercury becomes a sky-walker (*khecara*).
It should rotate clockwise; thus it becomes a "piercer of ten million" (*koṭivedhī*).
When the serpent has been consumed while still fresh, the mercury becomes a "piercer of ten" (*daśavedhī*);
when [the serpent] is twice [as much], it shall be a "piercer of a hundred" (*śatavedhī*); and when three times [as much], it pierces a thousand (*sahasrakam*).
O Goddess, [one should add] ten thousand to four times [the previous amount];

one should increase it in this sequence, with a progressive increase at each subsequent stage. Therein, one should digest the serpent (*pannaga*). Having digested the curved serpent, one should do so there according to that numerical sequence.
O Queen of the Gods, by that discourse the mercury becomes a "piercer of ten million" (*koṭivedhī*).
O Mistress of the Gods, the ash-mercury was consumed by Ruru, the lord of the Dānavas; therein, the sharp [mercury] was processed twelvefold.
Having consumed a single *pala* [of it], the Dānava, arrogant in his strength, uprooted the world and even pulverized Kailāsa. There,
having meditated for a moment, I beheld that which was wrought by his illusion.
The mercury was processed within a serpent and struck with an equal portion of mica. Anointed with that mercury, the trident was fashioned by the daughter of the snowy mountain;
by that trident, the Dānava who was arrogant in his strength was slain.
One should digest gold, copper, as well as *tīkṣṇa*, *vājara*, *paḍālaka*, *rohaṇa*, and *kāntaloha* according to the number of the principles (*tattva*).
Each one of these, when bound, makes this king of mercury attain the state of a sky-walker (*khecaratā*).

O Goddess, listen to how the digestion (*jāraṇā*) of the melted *gandhanāga* is easily accomplished: First, mercury that has been thoroughly purified should be combined with the powder of turmeric and rubbed until it turns black; then one should wash it with warm *kāñjika*.

Thus, being rubbed again and again, the scent-elephant (*gandhanāga*) will undergo liquefaction. O Goddess of the Gods, having repeatedly stirred the urine of an elephant, a calf, or a buffalo, one should sprinkle the serpent seven times.
Having made [the leaves] so that they can be pierced by a thorn, O beautiful one, one should apply sulphur to its petals in a measure equal to one-fourth [of the leaf]. Then,
having spread out a layer of lac, [one applies] the hairs immediately thereafter.
Above that, sulfur powder; then likewise, *nāgadalā*.
Sulfur, human hair, and a layer of lac—having spread these out in sequence and placed them above, one should fashion a wick with threads.
One should place that wick, with its tip blazing, in the midst of *karañja* oil for ten nights;
then one should hold it in pieces and cause that liquefied substance (*druti*) to fall into a vessel containing *sauvīra* and *ṭaṅkaṇa*.
O Dear One, one should place that oil inside a glass flask.
Having prepared a cow’s teat-shaped crucible and smeared it with stone,
O Goddess, one should determine the strength or weakness of the mercury by means of the sixty-fourth part and so forth.
Having added the *gandhanāga* flux, O Goddess worshipped by the gods,
place that crucible in a pit filled with cow dung and apply the *puṭapācana* method using two handfuls of dried cow-dung and husks.

One should administer [the medicine] when there is apprehension of indigestion; however, one should place four drops of the juice of *siṃhavallī* into the mouth as before. In this manner it should be done every day.
Through a threefold digestion (*jāraṇā*), the mercury becomes the color of a jambū fruit.

When the essence of honey is added little by little along with dead lead (*nāga*) until it is contained within the crucible, and glass is applied both below and above in this manner for twelve turns, it becomes well-blown and colored.
The roasted powder of seeds,
mixed with one-fourth part of mercury and ground with sour chickpea juice (*caṇakāmla*), will produce internal liquefaction (*garbhadruti*) in an instant.
O Goddess, if there is no internal liquefaction, [add] two parts of *varṇikā* and *gandha*.
A seed coated with a paste made from red sindūra, alarka, ṭaṅkaṇa, and āśugapuṅkha, and then subjected to *puṭa* firing, will become liquefied within its interior.
When the seed has been digested with parts equal to one-quarter or one-half [of the metal], it effects penetration (*vedha*).

Having sequentially added one-sixteenth and one-twentieth part [of mercury] to the three-fold *rīti* alloy, and having smeared this "Tārāriṣṭa" upon the silver with the remaining silver, one should perform the transmutation (*vedhana*) with that mercury.
Beyond this, O Goddess, I shall describe the refinement [of mercury] and the digestion of *nāga* and *abhra*. Having ground *manaḥśilā* and the red *karavīra*,
one should saturate it twenty times with the juice of *yavaciñcā*.
Having smeared it with that paste, one should carefully roll it into a leaf of *nāga* and cook it over fire until it becomes a powder. Then,
take three parts of mercury (*rasaka*) and one part of *darada*.

One should grind *pādagandha* and *śilāviṣa* with *mātuluṅga*. Having smeared a crucible (*mūṣā*) with this paste and subjected it to *puṭapāka*, one should then blow upon that lead (*nāga*); thus, after seven cycles, it becomes like gold.

Yellow mica (*pītābhraka*), however, consists of single layers; when heated in a crucible smeared with black pepper, it becomes fire-colored and should be cast into the juice of *saubhāñjana*. One should cause it to fall [into the crucible] according to the previous procedure; that essence (*sattva*) will shine like gold.
The leaf of *rañjitanāga* (tinted lead), the essence of yellow mica (*pītābhraka*), along with the smoke arising from a woman’s breast-milk and glass, *guñjā*, magnetite, and *ṭaṅkaṇa*,
combined with *tuttha*— this constitutes the dual combination (*dvaṃdvita*) of lead and mica.
Alternatively, one should grind mercury for three days with *kiṃvāra*, *nāla*, *siddhārtha*, *dhūmasāra*, brick, and jaggery, and then subject it to steaming in a *dolāyantra* for three days,
combined with a paste of *punarnavā*, *meṣaśṛṅgī*, and *sarpākṣī*.
Then, O Goddess of the Suras, one should again subject the *asurī* and river-venom (*sindhuviṣa*) to sweating for three days in a dolāyantra with ground black pepper;
having then administered *nāgābhra* in an eighth part [of the dose], one should cause it to be ingested.
One part consists of two portions of stone; there should be *sindhusauvarcala* salt. Half a *ṭaṅka* of poison and one-eighth of a ball of *viḍa* salt [should be added].
It is to be cooked for three days in a tortoise-shaped vessel (*kacchapa*). Thus, it is to be processed six times.
Stone, blue vitriol, mercury, copper, iron, bell-metal, brass, and gold—these, starting with vitriol, increase in sequence through the reduction of the essence of *tāpya* [calamine].
When only gold remains, that is the seed; it should be mixed with a quarter-part of *mātuluṅga* juice.
One should circulate the king of essences; one should digest it with those things containing gold.
Then, O Goddess of the Gods, having placed it in a *padma* apparatus along with calamine, black salt, realgar, sulphur, blue vitriol, and borax, and having inserted a pin, one should proceed.

One should gently heat it for three days until the seed becomes liquefied; that very mercury, once properly digested, remains motionless in the fire. Then, by means of the sixfold seed, the process of *sāraṇā* is performed according to the sequential method.

One should pierce copper with a thousandth part of *tārāriṣṭa* and *mahiṣa*. The mercury (*rasa*) proceeds when combined with a paste of *viṣa*, *gandhaka*, *tāpya*, *abhra*, crow-dung, *ghanadhvani*, *sahadevī*, and *vahniśikhā*. (RA 11.196–197)

The swooned mercury, the dead mercury, the leech-binding itself as the fourth, the form-binding, the cloth-binding as the fifth, the ash-mercury, and the *khoṭa*— thus mercury is sevenfold through its purification. (RA 11.198)
The mercury should have the color of a serpent; having abandoned excessive volatility, it is said to be "mūrchita" when its characteristic signs are observed:
moisture, density, brilliance, weight, and [controlled] volatility.

One should know that he in whom these are not seen is one who has undergone the impurity of death (*mṛtasūtaka*). Furthermore, that which is multicolored, clear, and quickly attaches itself to the womb like a leech— that is the characteristic of the attachment of a leech, which is the impurity of birth (*sūtaka*).
Heaviness and redness; by means of fire, it should remain held in the midst of a flame like the sun. This is the characteristic of the binding of the form (*mūrtibandha*).
Alternatively, through the incineration (*jāraṇā*) of a rod (*śalākā*), the state of being a bound form is desired.
White, yellow, and heavy, as well as soft and resembling beeswax—
if it remains in the midst of fire, these are the characteristics of a bound cloth (*paṭṭabandha*). Black, white, yellow, blue, and likewise ash-colored.

When fickleness has been destroyed, that is the characteristic of the reduced mercury (*bhasmasūta*). When the mercury resembles a hen’s egg and breaks like salt, the mercury (*rasa*) swirls in that manner; this is the characteristic of the solidified globule (*khoṭaka*).
Alternatively, for cutting, it should be unctuous; by means of a soft ray, the white, hard, and indestructible [substance] should melt. This is the characteristic of the *khoṭabandha*.
As for the five [substances] beginning with *khoṭa*, having set aside the leech-like form—
They are smelted in the fire of *haṭha*; once they have fainted, they do not remain [as they were].
Resembling the rising sun and possessing various colors, O Mistress of the Gods, the *rasabhairava*, having been colored, pierces the metals of the body.

Purification of the mercury (*sūtaka*) comes first; after that, the measurement of the dose, the digestion (*jāraṇa*) of the essence of *vyoma*, and the digestion of all essences. Following that, the internal and external liquefaction (*druti*), and then the digestion of gold.

Afterwards, the pouch of divine herbs; beyond that, the binding with jewels. Then, O Goddess, the coloring; and then the digesting, the following, and the transmuting should be administered to the mercury by the wise.

For one who knows this sequence in this way, there is accomplishment without a doubt. But for one who knows the piercing [technique] regarding the body, metals, and alchemy, birth, old age, and disease are destroyed; of this there is no doubt.

Within the body, however, there are five jewels: nāga, vaṅga, and likewise iron, which serve as the vehicle for the king of mercury (*rasarāja*) and as the medicine that destroys disease. By means of medicinal herbs, the mercury proceeds through the sequence of the power of its application.
It moves through the collection of diseases and devours malignant ailments. Having understood its movement, physicians should then treat it with that movement;
for without movement, mercury neither moves nor penetrates.
All diseases of the skin and blood would be rendered useless; the effort alone would be in vain.
Whatever medicinal formulation corresponds to a particular disease, one should apply that very same formulation together with Rasendra; it removes the ailments of men, elephants, and horses.
Āroṭa bestows strength; when rendered unconscious (*mūrchita*), it destroys disease;

when bound (*baddha*), it grants the perfection of *khecarī*; when killed (*mārita*), it brings about freedom from old age and death. Specifically, when rendered unconscious by means of sulfur (*gandhaka*), it pacifies diseases.
The mercury has been killed by the medicinal herb so that it may not live again. It permeates through metals; therefore, one should prepare an elixir (*rasāyana*) with it.
Tell me this, O Goddess of Gods! What else do you wish to hear?
The illustrious Goddess said:
"O Lord, what kind of herb is it that is auspicious and causes the intensification of the vital essence?"
By what means does the ash-born mercury arise? Or by what means is the binding of the *khoṭa* achieved?
Śrī Bhairava said:
Listen with care, O Bhairavī, to this secret of the binding of mercury.
O Goddess praised by heroes, this was not known even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the other lords of the gods.
Between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, there is a Rākṣasa named Prayoga;
O lady of excellent limbs, in his vicinity, a newborn child is bound [by death] in an instant.
The best of practitioners should take the leaves of the night-stalker;
when pressed beneath [the stone], O Goddess, the juice becomes excellent.
Having ground that very juice for three days, the alchemist [should proceed].
One should quickly bind the *āroṭa* [mercury] and dissolve the *gagana* [mica] therein.
By means of that very leaf-juice, one should further process the *gagana* seven times; then, it should be combined together with the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*).

O Goddess, when the mercury is in the yantra of the Vidyadhara, one should cause the sky to dissolve therein. O Mistress of the Gods, within a single month that [sky] is digested; when the mercury has been equally and completely digested, O Goddess, the mercury becomes a hundred-fold penetrator (*śatavedhī*).
O Goddess, one should then saturate the sulphur seven times with the juice of *dvipadī* and the essence of the night-walker (*niśācara*).
By applying it as a paste to silver leaves, there arises the most excellent gold, half-and-half.
When this sulfur has been completely digested, the mercury becomes a hundred-fold penetrator (*śatavedhī*).
Then, having added that same sulfur, one should remove the sun (*ravi*) by smearing it upon a leaf;
then, one should process that sun within silver (*tāra*) three times.
Gold mixed with half [the amount] of mercury attains equality with the *mātṛkā*;
then, having melted that very sulphur directly, make it flow quickly.
One should rub the lord of mercury (*rasendra*) with that, and thus cause its physical body to dissolve.
By that very same mere ointment, O beloved, it destroys the eighteen types of leprosy,
hemorrhoids, fistula-in-ano, spider-bites, and diseases of the head. The mineral calamine (*tālaka*) should be saturated seven times with the juice of the night-stalker (*niśācara*).

By that very [substance], one should cause the tin to be killed; the tin should then be extracted into silver. One should digest that silver in mercury; that mercury shall undergo fixation by mere smearing with that very [substance], and it becomes the sixty-fourth part [of its weight].

In the sixty-fourth part, one should cause the application of copper-mercury (*śulvavedha*); indeed, one should apply copper to silver (*tāra*). That silver becomes gold; that silver becomes most excellent, bestowing virtue (*dharma*), pleasure (*kāma*), wealth (*artha*), and liberation (*mokṣa*). (RA 12.15)
One should have the flowers of the night-stalker (niśācara) ground into a fine powder weighing ten palas, and then saturate it with the juices of the emblic myrobalan (dhātrī).
Having mixed it with ghee and honey, one should place it in a new vessel.
It should be placed within a heap of grain for twenty-one days, O Goddess of the Gods.
By merely consuming it, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
One should lick the fine powder of the bark mixed with honey.
Through practice for half a month, O beloved, this becomes manifest. By the use of its urine and feces for a full month, base metal becomes gold;
by the use [of these] for a month, even a serpent becomes gold.

Or one should take that oil produced from its fruit; with that oil in the apparatus known as *pātāla*, O Goddess of Gods, the wise man should cause the mercury to contract. At that very moment, O Goddess, the great mercury becomes bound in a cloth (*paṭṭabaddha*).
A pungent bracelet should be made; by that, O fair-faced one, the killing of the *rasaliṅga* is accomplished through contraction—a most wonderful feat to be performed.
[The mantra] cast seven times into the juice of a night-stalker [is for] the sun.
By that [process], it becomes free from blackness and arises with the luster of gold.

The external [substance] is equal to *tārā*; when sprinkled and sown by that, it pierces mercury (*sūta*) in a tenfold ratio; and when yellow [mercury] is treated with a hundred [parts], it pierces ten [times].

One hundred [times] pierces the *lakṣa*; one thousand [times] is a *koṭivedhaka*. A *koṭivedhi* should be ten parts; it is a *koṭivedhi* by means of an equal [amount]. (RA 12.26) Furthermore, I shall explain another: the binding of mercury (*rasabandha*), which is very difficult to obtain. (RA 12.27)

She who is the mother of the three worlds, the sovereign of herbs— by the mere contact of her [substance], mercury remains bound. Having been rubbed for seven days with the juice of that great herb, it [remains fixed].
By a penetration of even a hundredth part, it produces divine gold.
O lady of excellent complexion, by rubbing [the mercury] in that [substance] for fourteen days,
the mercury becomes a direct piercer of a hundred thousand (*lakṣavedhī*), turning the eight metals into gold.
O Goddess of the Gods, within three weeks it pierces ten lakhs;
indeed, in the fourth week, the great mercury becomes a "crore-piercer" (*koṭivedhī*). It is then sweated, heated, and rubbed with the juice of the great medicinal herb (*mahauṣadhī*).

She bestows the *siddhi* of the sky-farer; her range of movement becomes unimpeded. One may enjoy a thousand women within a single day, for one’s shadow vanishes and one becomes invisible, wandering through the three worlds by means of the elixirs.
By the very juice of the great medicinal herb (*mahauṣadhī*), the reviving of the dead occurs;
by this one should kill the mercury (*sūta*). O beloved, bring it to the five stages.
One should administer it as nasal drops (*nasya*) to the deceased and massage the hands and feet.

But his life-force may enter even one who is dead, O fair-faced one. Furthermore, I shall describe another method for the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to achieve: by means of the essence of human marrow alone, the quicksilver is bound in an instant.
Having added the juice of *narasāra* (human marrow), it attains a bond at the end of the day along with the dust of *dvipadī*; one may thus color all metals.
By means of the juice of *narasāra* alone, when [the mercury] has been digested six times over the course of six months (*ṣaḍguṇapannage*), [it becomes perfected].
O Goddess, one should likewise imagine that [mineral] as realgar (*manaḥśilā*), even if it is green or copper-colored.
It becomes odorless; however, that elixir (*rasāyana*) destroys [the poison] when combined with the dust of *dvipadī*. A snake becomes devoid of its vital essence (*niḥsattva*).

O Goddess, when the mercury has been digested with the essence of human marrow (*narasāra-rasa*) six times in lead (*tāra*), silver (*tāmra*), or even gold (*pannaga*), the mercury becomes capable of piercing ten million *koṭi*s.
The essence of human marrow is [taken] in breast milk; there are seven separate saturations (*bhāvanā*).

One should cause the king of mercury (*rasendra*) to swallow a morsel (*grāsa*) in the apparatus called Vidyādhara. O Goddess, O lady of beautiful countenance, the sky (*gagana*) is digested— even that which is "mouthless"—
by means of the essence of *narasāra* and the juice of *kīṭamārī*.
O Goddess, it causes the sky, sharp iron, and the serpent to melt. Through the essence of *narasāra* and the essence of *hanūmatī*,
divine gold is produced by means of *niṣeka*, O beloved of the Sun.

Having added *narasāra* juice, one should then grind *mañjiṣṭhā* and red sandalwood in their own juice; O Goddess, one should then sprinkle the serpent-metal (*pannaga*). Sprinkled seven times in that manner, it instantly becomes divine gold.
O Goddess, O Beloved, that serpent [mineral] should be rubbed with copper three times;
when joined with five parts of silver and one-eighth part of gold, it becomes like gold— an elixir for the work of gold-making.
One should saturate cinnabar seven times with the essence of human marrow;

with that very [essence], one should strike the sharp iron until it reaches the state of being reduced to ash. That ash, when ground together with copper, should be processed by means of three parts of that [copper].

That mercury, resembling gold, should be combined with silver in an eighth part; or else, silver and gold may be in equal parts, while the brass should be double that amount. It should then be processed seven times in the juice of *narasāra* and in *rasaka*.

That mercury (*rasa*) and *rasaka*, as well as sharp iron (*tīkṣṇaloha*) and *pannaga*— one should grind these together with the essence of human marrow (*narasārarasa*). By that alone, in a single moment, the binding (*bandha*) of both the mercury and the *rasaka* occurs.
Likewise, one should color sharp *nāga* and copper with mercury;
the whole becomes gold, shining like the flower of the *kūṣmāṇḍa*. I shall now further proclaim another [method], the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to obtain.
It is named Kaṅkālakhecarī, O Supreme Goddess. Having collected its oil, one should perform the medicinal saturation (*bhāvayet*) for one day with Māghakhecarī in a vessel made of glass (*bhāskara*).
When the second day has arrived, one should cause the diamond-jewel (*vajraratna*) to be struck [with a hammer] and then heat it in fire until it has the brilliance of a well-heated flame.
One should then soak that diamond-jewel in the oil of *kaṅkālakhecarī*.
When poured ten times, it indeed takes on the appearance of ash. That gold, having its seed cooked, should be made equal to that ash;
having added one-third part of *ṭaṅkaṇa*, one should blow it while it is placed in a blind crucible (*andhamūṣā*).

At that very moment, the pair unites: the diamond-gem and gold. O lady of noble hips, if the mercury that pierces ten million [times] dissolves silver and gold equally, O Goddess, it penetrates the eight metals.

I shall further proclaim another [method]: the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to attain. O Beloved, one should take a medicinal plant possessing seeds—certain shrubs and creepers known as *mantrasiṃhāsanī*; the second, O Goddess, is the *khecarī*.
One should take that oil in a copper vessel within the *pātālayantra*. Then,
O fair-faced one, one should place the juice of *khecarī* into the midst of that oil and set it in the center of the *medinīyantra*.
O Goddess, having first given the "sky" (mercury) on the surface of the earth as a swallow of mercury by means of that previous medicinal herb, make a ball (*golaka*) through kneading.
Having tied it in a small pouch (*poṭalikā*), one should digest the sky with that.
But when the sky has been fully digested, the mercury remains bound.
When it is blown upon with the blast of the bellows and heated,
its form— which is like crow-dung— perishes, and that which was equally digested becomes [pure].

When the sky has doubled and aged, one should collect the eight metals. (RA_12.64) Furthermore, I shall explain another [method]: the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to attain. (RA_12.65) There is a medicinal herb, *turasiṃhanī*, produced from the body of Śiva.
She indeed digests sulphur; she also digests orpiment.
She also digests gold; and she binds the lord of mercury. She indeed digests coral, and likewise causes the sky to melt.

She shall cause even a vajra to be destroyed and cause all beings to fall. O fair-faced one, having placed [the substance] in the juice of harīndarī on a cow’s horn, she shall digest all metals and even cook sentient beings.

It should be placed within a heap of grain; the impurity (*sūtaka*) remains until the [grain] has perished. O Goddess worshipped by the gods, when the mercury (*rasendra*) has been digested in equal amounts of divine medicinal juice and gold, it will penetrate ten *koṭis* [of times its weight].
In the fifth [stage], however, it is ten million lakhs; in the sixth, one pierces by touch;
in the seventh, one becomes a piercer by smoke; in the eighth, by sight;
and in the ninth, one becomes a piercer by sound. Beyond this, there is nothing further.
Deluded beings wander like cattle; for those devoid of the medicinal plants of the *kula*, no accomplishment whatsoever arises from the juices of ordinary grass-herbs.
Therefore, with every effort, one must recognize the medicinal plants of the *kula*.
The sixty-four divine medicinal herbs are established within the *kula*;
those fools do not know them at all, being deluded by the delusion of the gods. But the non-divine herbaceous plants grow in mountain caves.

O fair lady, mercury is never bound by the juice of grass-herbs; it remains inexhaustible and does not stay within the midst of fire. It neither becomes a *khoṭa* nor ash, nor does it turn into any other substance.
What substance could it possibly act upon? When being heated, it does not remain [in its original state].

O beloved, that mercury performs piercing (*vedha*) beyond a hundred times, whether in the leaf-process (*pattra*), the cooking-process (*pāka*), the *kaṭa*-process, or the cutting-process (*cheda*); it never remains as mere gold.

As long as even a single [unit] has not been bound— that gold which was sold for the sake of virtue, wealth, pleasure, and liberation— one should certainly not give it away, my dear. The Goddess said:
"The charioteer has become lifeless; how can one who is himself lifeless give life? How does he live, O Śaṅkara?
Śrī Bhairava said:
O Goddess, when the mercury has been rendered unconscious by a divine herb and the *sūta* is freed from *kālikā*, then, O Pārvatī,
it seizes the time of another; for mercury devoid of *kālikā* takes away [the life] of others.
It pacifies the impurities of all eight metals in an instant.
Who indeed would say that mercury has died when it has fallen into a great swoon? By the very essence of the divine medicine, it becomes restored to consciousness.
The mercury, consisting of the five elements, remains as Sadāśiva himself. (RA_12.83) Again, O Goddess, I shall explain another matter: the binding of mercury.
By this very [process], gold is produced from iron struck by a thunderbolt. (RA_12.84)

Vajra-ash and gold-ash—one should bind those together in one place. It should be digested in the juice of *niśācara*; one should digest that mercury with human life-force (*narajīva*), O auspicious lady, and kill it with the divine medicinal herbs of *gajāri*.
He by whom that essence has been consumed is himself Sadāśiva manifest.
By consuming even a single *tolaka* of it, a man becomes one who effects transmutation through touch (*sparśavedhī*). From the sweat of his body, the king of essences (*rasarāja*) is transmuted.

Even from perspiration, [it is extracted] by means of urine. The eight metals and gold—[attained through this], that best of practitioners, possessing the luster of Prajāpati and the brilliance of Kṛṣṇa, shall live for eight hundred thousand years. In an instant, he binds the mercury (*sūtaka*).
O Goddess, by touching it with the enemy of elephants (the lion), it is bound by the protector of the earth (mercury).

O Dear One, when the sky (mercury) has been processed with the juice of the *vajravallī* creeper, one should digest it in a sand-vessel (*vālukāyantra*); it becomes a solid bolus (*khoṭa*) at that very moment.

Having combined one *māṣa* of a dead globule (*mṛtagolaka*) with one *māṣa* of a golden globule (*hemagolaka*) and thoroughly rubbed them together with lime juice (*luṅgāmla*) for three days, one should coat the leaves of lead (*nāga*) weighing one *karṣa* with this medicinal paste.
One should wrap it with *vṛścikālī* and then smear that paste;
thus, O Goddess, one may kill a serpent. It will become like a *śakragopa* insect.
One *karṣa* of silver leaves should be smeared with the dead serpent.
Then one should smear that leaf with *vṛścikālī* and wrap it around.

O Goddess, that silver (*tāra*) dies [is killed], becoming like the red glow of vermilion (*sindūra*). With a thousandth part of that very [substance], one should effect the transmutation (*vedha*) of copper (*śulba*).

Divine gold is produced, serving as an ornament for the gods' jewelry. O Pārvatī, the plant known by the name Caṭulaparṇī— which possesses milky sap, bears many fruits, and has knotted stems— is praised for the binding of mercury.

In the juice of *ekavīrā* root, one should blow upon the mercury placed in a sealed crucible (*mūkamūṣā*) using the breath from the mouth; thus bound, it is recommended for consumption. Furthermore, the root of *raktakañcukī*, ground with breast milk...
In a crucible, by means of the previous method, one effects the binding of mercury.
One should blow upon the seed of *vṛścikāpattrikā* combined with women’s milk as before, for the alchemist’s purpose of consuming [the mercury].

Taking the *vajrakanda* root, one should cast it into the midst of the mercury; having applied the *puṭa* known as "Lord of Elephants" (*gajendra*), one should bring it to a state of being bound seven times. A wise person should consume that mercury, and within six months he shall become immortal.
Taking the tuber of *lāṅgalī* and the tuber of *karkoṭī*, having placed the mercury in their midst, one should heat it and then grind it again.
It dies; of this there is no doubt, when it has been smelted with a fierce fire.
The mercury placed within the beak of a parrot should then be enclosed and heated.

This agent of penetration, when used at a hundredth part [of the dose], will bring about the perfection of the body. One should place mercury with the juice of *haṃsapādī* inside the bulb of a porcupine.

One should administer the *gajendrapuṭana* [preparation]; one dies [of the disease], there is no doubt about this. (RA 12.106) Having taken *haṃsāṅghri* and *śukatuṇḍī*, one should grind the juice and place it inside the belly of a *krauñca* bird; then one should apply three *puṭa* [firing cycles]. (RA 12.107)
He dies; of this there is no doubt. This great elixir is the "piercer of a hundred thousand.
It is known as *tṛṇajyoti* ("grass-light"); listen, O beloved, to this divine herb. O Pārvatī, it burns constantly at night, but it does not burn during the day.
O Dear One, milk placed at its root becomes blood-red. By means of the juice and scent of that root combined with mica (*abhra*), ground with the sour juice of *mātuluṅga*,
a copper leaf smeared [with this] becomes gold after three *puṭa* applications.
O Goddess of the Suras, the king of mercury, when combined with the powder of its root and rubbed in the juice of *mātuluṅga*,
causes mica to dissolve in an instant.
Now, O Beloved, I shall explain *uccaṭī*, which binds the mercury.
The stalk alone would not be sufficient; its sheath is made of hair.
At its tip there is a flower resembling the beak of a parrot, and its petals, O Goddess of Gods, resemble the plumage of a parrot.
That bulb has the appearance of *kuṣṭha* and its milk resembles vermilion. O Pārvatī, if one takes that water which flows out like beeswax,
it pierces all metals, and they become gold.
One should grind mercury, orpiment, and blue vitriol with the juices of *uccaṭī*;
heated in the sun, the mercury dies through the power of the divine herb. O fair-faced one, it pierces the seven metals by means of a millionth part [of its weight].
Now, O beautiful goddess, I shall explain the ritual procedure for red *snuhī*:
one should apply a leaf-ointment of copper with the milk of *snuhī*,
and then heat it in the milk seven times, O lady of excellent countenance.
It should be stirred until it possesses a luster equal to that of Jāmbūnada gold.
Then, one should cook it with sesame oil for three days;
likewise, when the leaves of copper are pierced [with this], they become Jāmbūnada gold.
The juice is the latex of *raktasnuhī*; *kunaṭī* is sulphur and mica;
and *darada* is mercury. One should pierce [the metal] with iron by means of a thousandth part [of these].
Having taken the latex of *snuhī*, one should combine both it and gold for half a night.
Take realgar and fragrant powder; one should grind everything together in one place.
By this very method, one should purify gold for half a night.
Having fashioned it into a pill with that [substance], it pierces lead at that very moment.
Now, therefore, listen to the ritual for the divine herb *sthalapadminī*.
It resembles a lotus in its leaves and likewise in its flowers;
when broken, it yields milk that is of a beautiful red color.

Having stepped upon it with the left foot, one should behold the circle of the sky and behold it joined with the stars— the mandala of planets and constellations from a distance of a hundred thousand yojanas, O Goddess; that is to be known as the terrestrial lotus-pond.
Taking its five components— combined with mercury and sulfur (*haragaurī*), joined with realgar (*manaḥśilā*) and orpiment (*tāla*), and mixed with honey—
one should grind them for seven nights; with that, one should transmute copper (*śulva*).

O Goddess of the gods, gold becomes pierced by even a thousandth part of it. Having taken its five limbs, O beloved, one should cause the king of alchemical elixirs (*sūtarāja*) to circulate according to the previously mentioned procedure, and then blow it while it is contained within a sealed crucible (*mūkamūṣā*).
It dies amidst the *mūṣikā* [minerals] due to contraction; of this there is no doubt.
By that very means, one should pierce all metals with a thousandth part.
Now, therefore, O beloved, I shall fully explain the procedure for *kumudinī*.

Having split [the stone] from a Kāśmīra rock, one should perform [the rite] on the full moon day. Taking its five parts, one should then refine realgar (*manaḥśilā*) by holding it in a shallow pan (*kharpara*), refining it again and again.
Lead melted in an iron pan—make it combined with its own paste until it becomes equal to liquid saffron;
gold is certainly produced.
(RA_12.131) I shall now explain briefly how the *citraka* [pigment] is to be extracted. (RA_12.132)

Citraka is known to be of three kinds: red, black, and white; the black is for rejuvenation (*rasāyana*), while the white is for the alleviation of disease. These are ranked as superior, middling, and inferior.
A wise person should not uproot the black, red, or white variety during the winter season.
Having uprooted the black *citraka*, O Goddess, the milk that has not been smelled by cows and is situated within milk will instantly become black in color.
One should grind mercury together with the powder of its five parts.
And one should blow [the fire] in a mute crucible; the *khoṭa* [pill] becomes [ready] at that very moment.
Having put on red garments, with red garlands and ointments, on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, [one should offer] red *śāli* rice.
Having offered the oblation, O Great Goddess, one should extract red *citraka*.
By means of the powder of red *citraka* and three successive heats of tin,
[the mercury] is freed from all defects and becomes immobilized at that very moment.
Its root and *sūtaka* [mercury] are treated with sour substances; by using *kaṅguṇī* oil twenty-one times, the copper (*śulva*) will become pure.
When smeared with the oil of red *citraka* and *bhallātaka*, it is then subjected to the *puṭa* process.

O Goddess of gods, the leaf of *candrārka* becomes beautiful gold. By applying a paste of *nāginī* root, mercury (*sūtendra*), and red *citraka* in the same proportion as the leaf, *candrārka* becomes gold.
Combined with red *citraka*, even the elixir (*rasa*) will be effective at all times. (RA_12.142) O Pārvatī, listen as I describe the procedure for *jyotiṣmatī* oil.
(RA_12.143) There is a creeper named *jyotiṣmatī* which resembles gold in color.
Abounding with spreading creepers, auspicious with fruits the color of gold;
having taken the supreme seed during the first fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha,
one should boil it like sesame seeds, using either the hands or even the feet.
Having taken its oil, one should pour it into a copper jar. One should heat the jar while it is buried in the ground, gradually with a fire of husks;
when six months have passed, that jar shall become gold.
Having fashioned that [substance] out of gold and mixed it with oil and honey, one should pour it over the powder; the gold will become equal to copper.
Likewise, it shall pierce through a hundred [layers]; this is the unsurpassed jewel of knowledge.

I shall describe the *dagdhārohā*, O beloved; it brings about the binding of mercury (*rasabandha*) and should be known as that which effects touch-transmutation (*sparśavedha*), accomplishing all purposes and goals.
O Great Goddess, it may be cut by weapons or burnt by fire.
The divine great medicinal herb, though burnt and severed, sprouts in an instant.
Its flowers are produced in red, yellow, white, and black;
one should observe its well-formed leaves, which resemble those of the chickpea plant.
She resides on the bank of the Gomatī, at Arbuda on the Gaṅgā,
to the south of Ujjayinī, and is seen in the forest regions.
Her divine cave is endowed with black streaks.

Having combined it with betel leaf, the wise one should have it made into pills. By piercing all metals while they are molten in the midst of fire a thousand times, he turns them into gold in an instant.

In the same way, the mercury dies; when combined with *kāntaloha*, gold, and mica, it produces divine gold for the adornment of the ornaments of the gods. O Goddess, hear now of the divine herb renowned as *kaṭutumbī*. (RA 12.155–156)
Having collected its seeds, one should have them ground into a fine powder. It should be infused twenty-one times with the juice of *dhātrī* together with milk, combined with *viśvabheṣaja*.

Having cast the seed into the apparatus, the wise one should collect the oil and cause the mercury to coagulate with it; he should then rub it with *cakramarda*. [He should add] cow-bile and peacock-bile, combined with *kāṅkṣī* and *kāsīsa*.

These are equal in potency to mercury; for all of them, the impurity (*sūtaka*) is the same. It should be placed in a ram's horn and continuously sprinkled with a metal rod for one month; it will then pierce all metals.

Sulfur [is processed] with an iron rod; twenty-one times impregnated, iron is joined with this very [substance]. Combined with the juice of *jambīra* fruit, together with its seed and endowed with mercury (*sūtaka*), it is placed inside a sealed crucible (*andhamūṣā*).
For one month buried in the earth, it transforms the silver into gold. One should combine one part of the leaf, five parts of silver,
five parts of copper, and one part of the seed.
These shall be twelve parts. One should place all of that upon the earth for the consecration of this site, and have it prepared with the *bhūdaṇḍa* [mantra].
At the end of twenty-five days, the finest gold is produced.

I shall describe the procedure for the milk-yielding tuber (*kṣīrakanda*), which brings about all accomplishments and is supreme; therein, the red tuber is praised. When broken, this [tuber] exudes milk that is blood-red and very beautiful.
With seven leaves, glossy like the *snuhī* plant, resembling clouds in their resonance, adorned with beautiful golden luster,
this is the binding of the king of essences (*rasarāja*), which brings all sentient beings under control.
Having collected its milk, the wise man should extinguish the *tāra* and then blow upon it with a fire of *dhava* wood; thus, beautiful gold is produced.
[One should treat it] with the sap of *tintiṇī* leaves combined with a small amount of copper dust.
The wise one should rub the mercury; the binding of the mercury will occur.
Having cast it into the midst of water, the pill will become like a diamond.
O Goddess of the Gods, having squeezed out the excellent juice of the Śāka tree...
Combined with red sandalwood, one should digest all metals.
By means of the scent of sulphur (gandhapāṣāṇa), one should apply it to iron;
then all metals will mingle and flow like water.

Sulphur, calamine, and pyrite; mercury combined with red sandalwood and the juice of *rudantī*—this becomes silver and gold. One should [take] the resin of the *śāka* tree and strain it upon its own leaf.
One should grind the powder of the root of *śigru* with its own juice. Having smeared copper leaves with this and placed them in a crucible (*puṭa*), one should heat them;
that will quickly become divine gold, endowed with all auspicious characteristics.
The wise one should collect the ripe fruits of the *śākavṛkṣa* tree; having prepared them with its juice, he should infuse it for seven nights.
Then, combined with that same juice and likewise mixed with *mañjiṣṭhā*, [he should proceed].
One should smear the silver leaves; when heated, they become gold.
Next, I shall describe the procedure for the great medicinal plant *devadālī*:
it is white for the destruction of diseases, and black or yellow for the practice of *rasāyana*.
On the full moon day, on the thirteenth day, when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu,
or on the fifth day of the dark fortnight— one should extract this according to the prescribed ritual.
O Goddess, [the substances are] the fruit of *devadālī*, *viṣṇukrāntā*, and *sūtakam*.

It causes [the metal] to swoon and quickly binds it; it turns copper into gold. Having ground the fruit and root of *devadālī* together with the juice of *īśvarī* in water, one arrests tin in an instant.
Henceforth, O beloved, I shall explain the ritual for white guñjā.
On the fourteenth or the eighth day of the dark fortnight, O worshipper of the gods,
one should place earth in a skull and sprinkle it with water.
The seeds are those of the white guñjā; one should sow them with the flower [offering] using the mantra to be described hereafter. Likewise, one should perform the collection [of the seeds]:
*namo bhagavati śvetavalli śvetaparvatavāsini sarvakāryāṇi kuru kuru apratihate namo namaḥ svāhā* || 12.185 ||
Success is proclaimed by this mantra; it does not happen otherwise.
Likewise, within six months, one should protect the creeper purified by the mantra. Having taken pure copper, one should place it inside a crucible.
But when the amount numbering three and five *palas* is combined in one place with half a *karṣa* of white *guñjā*, it becomes *tāra*. That [silver] is devoid of odor;
when joined with the method of Brahmā (*brahmarīti*), the powder of *guñjā* is mixed together with it.
O Goddess, beautiful gold becomes the ornament of the gods. O Mistress of the Gods, I shall now describe the binding of mercury using moon-water.
On the full-moon day of the bright fortnight, having beheld the orb of the full moon...
They emerge, piercing the earth, as many streams of moon-water. Some are the color of clay; some are salty in taste;
some are equal to the moon; and some possess the luster of the sky.

They increase with the waxing of the moon, but they diminish with its waning. Having seen the water of the moon, especially on the full moon day, the practitioner of mantra beholds it emerge from the earth; it increases as the moon increases.
Having first established the boundary of the sacred field (*kṣetrabandha*) and worshipped the god Śaṅkara,
the wise practitioner, having fasted for a day and night and having honored that field on the fourteenth lunar day, should present an offering (*bali*) there.
On the full moon night,
having gone into his presence and taken up the "moon-water," one should stir it with honey and clarified butter while reciting the well-mantraed spells; then, being composed, one should drink it.
By merely drinking that very [substance], fainting occurs at that instant;
then, when the rising moon is seen, one should have milk given to him.
Through its application for seven nights, he becomes as stainless as the moon.

In twenty-one nights, by employing [this] for one month, he shall live for three days of Brahmā; that man shall attain the lifespan of Brahmā. One should grind mercury, gold, and the sky with lunar water.
When heated within a crucible, it becomes a pill at that very moment.
By its mere touch, this [pill] penetrates the eight types of base metals. The mercury should be processed with its juice, having been thoroughly fused with diamond.

In a pill [weighing] one-sixty-fourth part, there is a thousandfold [potency]. When doubled, it is a thousand. A man who places in his mouth a dose of mercury the size of a *guñjā* seed, bound with ten *saṃkalikās* and encased in the three metals, shall attain invisibility.
Oṃ, homage to Rudra, whose fangs are formidable, the destroyer of obstacles! Protect, protect the cardinal directions; protect, protect the intermediate directions! Rudra commands: huṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Rudra, who holds a trident in his hand, born from nectar! Protect, protect! phaṭ svāhā!
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the binding of the scissors-liquid (kartarī-rasa). (RA 12.201)
During the encounter with the Asuras, the great discus Sudarśana was hurled by the enemy of Mura with a mind possessed by wrath;
then, drops of sweat fell from his forehead.
Those divine [beings] fell to the ground and became the essence of scissors.
There, the Sudarśana discus, equal to the discus of Viṣṇu, was stationed for the sake of protection;
it revolves and cuts down weapons.
She utters thunderous roars and emits smoke and flames;
by the mere sight of her, she is the Scissors of Sight. Likewise, there is another, the Scissors of Sound.
She is the Scissors of Touch, the Scissors of Shadow, and the Scissors of Smoke.
That flame is indeed the scissor; the power of Ghorā is the scissor. For the sake of the welfare of the worlds, the power of Ghorā is established;
the Great Ghorā, whose form is the essence (*rasa*), is the cutter of those who have not attained success.

When one goes to her field (*kṣetra*), one should then recite the *aghora* weapon-mantra (*astra*) and again install the *ghora* [mantra] there; then the wise one should install the weapon-mantra by way of both direct and reverse order, having established the *kartarī* within the body.
One should seal that [deity] with the mudrā joined with the Aghora-weapon mantra.
One should worship her with a lamp and immobilize her with incense.
With the Viṣṭara-mudrā, one should apply the yoga of placement.
The *kañcukī* plant is *śilākrāntā*; the *kumārī* is *vajrakandaka*;
the blood of a woman and cow urine [are used for] the *tilaka*, which brings all under control.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the binding of poison with the juice of the *udara*.

Poison-water is equal to poison; ghee-water is like ghee, rich with white, yellow, and other colors, and that, O Goddess, is the supreme flavor. Having gone there to a forest region, one should recollect the thousand-fold formidable [mantra].
When hair is thrown into it, it bursts apart; one's own shadow is not seen. The oil takes on the shape of a ball, and the ghee spreads out;
it removes the scent of fragrant substances, and becomes salty and sour.
Having obtained [the ingredients], one should place the poisonous water and sulfur upon a leaf of the *pālāśa* tree; the seed of *harā* should be equal in measure to that.
Having ground them with goat’s milk, one should smear the copper leaves.
And by means of that crucible, O Mistress of the Gods, one should pierce all metals with a hundredth part [of the elixir], which resembles vermilion in its ruddy hue.
By this method, O Goddess, lead (nāga) attains the state of vermilion.

In this manner, one should cause the piercing of the *tāra* [crystal] with a thousandth part of that very [substance]. Red, yellow, and likewise black [piercings] perform increasingly superior effects. Alternatively, [one may place it] in a vessel of *kāntaloha* or even in a vessel made of gourd.
Having taken it as before with leaves, one should wrap it on the outside with *pālāśa* leaves.
One should place it upon a heap of grain for twenty-one days,
and then one should prepare a single drop in the midst of buffalo milk.
O Goddess, whoever should eat milk-rice mixed with honey and clarified butter, for as many palas of powder as there are, he shall live for a number of years equal to the number of those drops.
[One should take] lāṅgalī, house-soot, vermilion, and the two types of turmeric.
Meṣaśṛṅgī and Śṛṅgī, as well as Kṛṣṇonmatta and Māraka; likewise,
the mercury (sūtaka) together with its seed-substance,
should be ground by the wise man with poison-water and infused seven times with that same poison-water.
Alternatively, one should saturate that [substance] until it becomes a powder;
having mixed the nāga with that [powder], it should be prepared in a sixteenth part [of the dose].
One should saturate it three times in a crucible known as a *mūṣā* and in a bamboo-tube apparatus (*veṇuyantra*).
One should avoid its smoke, for it is extremely harmful to the limbs. Then, one should place *nāgasindūra* in a vessel made of gourd;
subsequently, one should pierce silver leaves with a powder of that substance in the proportion of one hundredth part.
Taking poison and water, one should pour them into a beautiful vessel of barley-gruel;
when poured into that vessel, it becomes a brilliant and auspicious pearl. Taking poison and water, one should cast them into the finest broth.
Realgar, sulphur, poison, borax, and lāṅgalī, ground into a fine paste in a mortar,
should be smeared upon silver leaves. When heated in a sealed crucible (andhamūṣā),
it becomes seedless gold.
Oṃ śrīnīlakaṇṭhāya ṭha ṭhaḥ. One should recite this ten thousand times.
I shall now describe the ritual for poison-grass; listen with a concentrated mind. (RA_12.229)
Take *gandha*, *mākṣīka*, and *darada*, combined with *kunaṭī* and *rasa*,
and mixed with *viṣatṛṇa*; having rubbed these with the acid of *mātuluṅga*,
apply this paste, measuring one *pala*, as an ointment upon the medicinal herb.
One should perform the *puṭa* process using the resin (*niryāsa*); thus gold becomes beautiful after three cycles.
Now, O Pārvatī, I shall describe the procedure for the water of Saṃjīvanī;
formerly, O Goddess worshipped by the gods, I was propitiated by Śukra.
For the benefit of the Dānavas who had perished in the battle with the gods,
I bestowed the *saṃjīvanī* lore in the form of water; by it,
those Daityas who died in the battle with the gods were restored to life.

She has been placed in the world of mortals; I shall relate it to you correctly. There exists in the mortal realm, in the highly meritorious and sacred southern region, a river named Godāvarī, as renowned as the Jāhnavī.
And on its southern bank is the city of Kadalīnagara;
to the south of that is a mountain renowned throughout all the worlds by the name Kṛṣṇagiri, which is seen to be auspicious in every way.

There is a village in the vicinity named Suprasiddhāmbikā. Having observed water there as well, one should examine it in a place honored by the gods. Then, having taken a dry bamboo cane, one should throw it into the middle of the water.

It becomes green and glossy; within a day and night, it certainly releases sprouts and leaves, appearing most enchanting. Then, with an offering of oblations and flowers, one should worship the Goddess.
[One should worship] Gaṇeśa, the lord of the field, as well as Caṇḍayonīśvara. I shall proclaim his mantra, which is difficult to obtain in the three worlds:
Oṃ, to Caṇḍa, the wielder of the Pināka bow, the one with a trident in hand; Oṃ, bind the cardinal directions, bind the intermediate directions! Ṭhaṭhaḥ.
Having consecrated sesame seeds, rice grains,

and mustard seeds seven times with this mantra, the practitioner should scatter them in the directions. With a concentrated mind, he should place water in a bitter gourd that has been protected by a ritual defense.

Having taken that with diligence, one should resort to one's own place. Having consecrated it seven times with this mantra over the water: *Oṃ namo 'mṛte amṛtarūpiṇi amṛtaṃ me kuru kuru evaṃ rudra ājñāpayati svāhā*.
Likewise, one *māṣa* of gold should be ground with that juice for one day; the wise man should drink it. Then, for twenty-one nights, he should diligently subsist on a diet of milk.
He shall live for more than ten thousand aeons, able to assume any form at will and possessed of great strength.
Having traveled a hundred yojanas, he returns once again;
invulnerable to all beings, that sky-walker moves according to his own will.
One should combine gold, mercury, and *vyoma* (aerial substance) in equal parts in a single place,
rub them with that liquid, and subject them to heat (*sveda*) seven times.
That mercury will transmute all metals by means of a sixtyth part [of its own weight].
Alternatively, one should consume that divine mercury together with honey for a period of only one month; by this practice, one may live for ten thousand Brahma-days.
Through its urine, excrement, and sweat, base metal becomes gold.
Having taken water in a windless place, one should drink three handfuls (*añjali*).
Immediately upon drinking it, fainting will occur; recovery of health shall come after three *praharas*.
In this manner for twenty-one days, one should thereafter subsist on a diet of milk.
Having the appearance of an eight-year-old, wise, able to assume any form at will, and possessing great strength,
he beholds the entire earth with all its seven netherworlds;
invulnerable to gods and daityas, he is born with a lifespan lasting for an eon.
Alternatively, taking water, mercury, and realgar, one should grind them on a stone mortar; it will then become a "lost-paste" (*naṣṭapiṣṭa*).
One should then subject it to sweating for seven nights and encase it with the three metals.
He shall vanish in an instant and become a lord of the Vidyādharas,
surrounded by a hundred perfected maidens for as long as fourteen kalpas.
During all those days, one should offer boiled śāli rice with ghee.
And combined with milk; one should always act in this manner.
I shall now explain the rule for warm water; listen with a concentrated mind.
Wherever one perceives warm water, there one should make one's dwelling.
There is a river named Godāvarī, highly renowned in Mahārāṣṭra; on its northern side stands the Sahya mountain, a sacred peak. Therein lies the famous temple known as Mātāpura.
Therefore, O Goddess, to the north lies the supreme city called Kampā.
There resides the deity Kampeśvara; there is also the constant hot spring and the river named Praṇītā. Having bathed there, the best of practitioners [attains success].

Afterwards, one should perform the rite as prescribed in a pit of hot water. Having stayed there for a night, a wealthy person should consume [the substance] day by day for exactly one month; he shall live for eight hundred years.
If one practices this for one year, one shall live happily for ten thousand years,
free from wrinkles and grey hair, possessing enjoyments like Indra himself. If one drinks only water for one year, one shall live as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.
By means of its urine and excrement, copper becomes gold.
One should add hot water, green vitriol (*kāsīsa*), combined with sulphur (*gandhapāṣāṇa*), along with one-fourth part of *rasaka*, and cast it into ten parts [of the metal]. (RA 12.265–266)
One should grind all the copper together until it becomes a fine paste (*naṣṭapiṣṭa*).
By merely smearing it with that, the copper becomes gold.
When it has been poured with that water, the wise one should apply a secondary coating (*prativāpa*).

And copper becomes gold, possessing the brilliance of the rising sun. When that water is poured over gold combined with the essence of seed, and silver is likewise poured over by this same method, it attains the state of gold.
One should consume *bhallātaka* with warm water and sesame paste;
by practicing this for two months, one shall live for three hundred years. [The ingredients are:
mercury, *gandhāśman*, *rasaka*, *tuttha*, *darada*, and *mākṣika*.
Having rubbed it with warm water in a crucible, one should smear the copper leaves.
O Goddess, one should heat them twice; thus, O Mistress of the Gods, by this sequence, copper becomes fourteen-carat.
By this same sequence, O Goddess, copper becomes sixteen-carat.

One part each of gold and silver, and two parts each of *kāntaloha* and mica, should be ground separately with warm water; through smelting, they will attain the state of a solid bolus (*khoṭa*). One should hold that in the mouth for a month, and the man shall become one with a diamond body (*vajrakāya*).
One should consume that powder, the size of a barley grain, with honey and clarified butter;
when one *pala* of it has been consumed, his excretions become gold. One should eat horse-gram boiled in hot water and subsist on milk.

One should perform a bath with warm water; [this grants] a lifespan of a hundred years for every year [of practice]. One should boil milk, warm water, and a decoction of *triphalā* together in a vessel made of *kānta* iron, and consume that *pāyasa* for one month.
Having eaten this, one may live for a hundred kalpas; such a man shall possess the lifespan of Viṣṇu.
Hereafter, O beloved, I shall explain the procedure for *śailodaka* (rock-water), which is of four kinds: *kardama* (mud), *āpaḥ* (water), *mahīśaila* (earth-rock), and *śila* (stone).
Some pierce in a single moment; some pierce in a day;
others on the earth pierce in a fortnight, a month, or up to six months. When a piece of wood is thrown, it is seen to become as solid as a stone.
O Goddess of gods, that which acts both externally and internally is proclaimed as the "penetrator" (*vedhaka*).
Cinnabar, yellow orpiment, sulfur, and realgar—
that which removes the odor from these is also a "penetrator."
One should throw sulphur and realgar into a jar filled with water;
when it takes the form of bubbles, then it becomes "mountain-water" (*śailodaka*);
otherwise, O Goddess, it is merely a coating and should not be taken, as it is useless. (RA 12.281)

On Śrīśaila, at the edge of the Śrī forest, on the stone slab known as Paryaṅka, it pierces in an instant; on the bank of the river Bhagavatī, it pierces there in a single day; but at Gokarṇa, it takes three days.
At Bhadrāṅga, it shall last for nine days; at Tristhalānta, for three days;
at Dhāreśvara, it shall last for a fortnight; and at Varṣāpurī, for one day.
At Brahmeśvara, it shall last for a month; but at Vyāghrapurī, it lasts for one day.

At Aghoreśa, however, it is monthly; likewise at Siṃhadvīpa; furthermore, for one day at Brahmagiri; but at Vindhya, it is instantaneous piercing. At Mālyavant, it is daily; the water from the rock is instantaneously piercing.
On the delightful Kiṣkindhyā mountain, on the bank of the Pampā, there is grass and water;
two yojanas further to the west of that, O Goddess, there is a hill on the ground at that very place. I shall pierce through the mountain in three days.

In the city of the Goddess on Mount Sahya, in the vicinity of Kṣīrakṣetra, there is Śailodaka, which pierces a target at a distance of ten million [yojanas]. Even in a difficult region, in the city named Gokula, there is that of Nṛsiṃha, which pierces a target at a distance of one hundred thousand [yojanas] in a single day.
Elsewhere, wherever it may be—whether arising from Brahmā, Viṣṇu, or Śiva, that nectar is present there as well. This is the supreme method of vajrification.
(RA 12.288) I shall explain its origin so that practitioners may understand it. (RA 12.289)
From the sweat that fell from the body of the Boar as he lifted up the earth, there arose the most excellent mountain-water;
it became momentary in his mouth, but lasted for a full day in the region of his snout.
With the two arms, it should pierce through three days; with the sides, it pierces for six months, as does the other limb. All of these yield equal results.
Having performed the protection of that field with the Aghora weapon, one should offer the bali-oblation to the directions.
Having offered a hundred thousand [repetitions] and performed the recitation, one should take up the supreme nectar.
O worshiper of the gods, during autumn, summer, spring, or winter,
[one should do so] in an iron vessel, a copper vessel, or a vessel made of gourd.
One should add eight *pala*s of rock, water, and lotus, as well as one *pala* of milk.
Having boiled it until only the milk remains, a person who drinks this for twenty-one days will live for a thousand years, free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Alternatively, one should take eight palas of milk mixed with one pala of water and consume it until only the milk remains; one obtains the fruit previously described.
Or, one should boil eight parts of water with kulattha beans until only one-eighth remains.
One should cook clarified butter with four times that amount [of the aforementioned ingredients] until only the ghee remains. Bṛhaspati says that one should lick it mixed with honey for three weeks;
O Goddess, within a month, having understood the strengths and weaknesses of the scriptures, one attains mastery over them.
Having the appearance of one sixteen years of age, he will live for a thousand years; of this there is no doubt.

Furthermore, one should eat the remaining kulattha beans mixed with honey and ghee in a quantity equal to one-fourth [of the usual portion] for one year; by this, one lives for ten thousand years within a month.
One should perform an oil massage with that perfected oil and also carry out rubbing for one month; thereafter, once rubbed, it brings about the perfection of the body and swiftly conquers scabies,
eczema, ringworm, and leprosy.
He becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair, and lives for a thousand years.
(RA_12.300) He who, having risen in the morning, drinks three mouthfuls of mountain water, shall live for a thousand years, freed from wrinkles and grey hair, after six months. (RA_12.301)
Alternatively, O Goddess, one should grind the *sūtaka* with water;
after one month, O Mistress of the Gods, it will become a "lost-powder" (*naṣṭapiṣṭa*).
One should consume it for just one month; he shall become free from old age and death.

Alternatively, one should grind that mercury with gold; then, the powerful [alchemist] should mix it with that liquid and heat it in a fire of *khadira* wood. This pill, named Sundarī, wards off all weapons.
The self-established agent and destroyer shall live as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure. Iron pyrite, mica, and realgar, as well as gold and silver—
all of these should be cooked with milk and wine for three days.
By using it for only one month, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair. (RA 12.306) Then, with that very water, one should cook milk-rice (*pāyasa*) with half as much milk;
by using it for only one month, wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed. (RA 12.307)
Having cooked sixty *pathyā* fruits in that water, one should mix three hundred and sixty measures of honey and place the entire contents in a vessel on the ground.
Rising each morning, one should consume it one measure at a time, day by day.
Freed from wrinkles and graying hair, he shall live for a thousand years.
(RA_12.309) Or, having become as hard as stone, he may eat *kulattha* beans with honey and clarified butter;
by consuming them for six months, he shall live for a thousand years. (RA_12.310)

Having prepared a *kūṣmāṇḍa* fruit that has been "slain," one should eat whatever fruits and metals have been cast into water and have become solidified like stone, while subsisting on a diet of milk until the end of digestion; thus the man shall possess a body as indestructible as a diamond (*vajrakāya*).
Having ground it with that water, one should boil the mica, O Dear One;
by consuming it combined with the three pungents, one shall live for a thousand years. Alternatively, one should grind one karṣa of mercury with that same water.
That which is situated within the fruit of the *iṅgudī* tree, located in the midst of mountain water, becomes solid after exactly three times that period.
It should be held in the mouth for six months; it makes the body like adamant.
He possesses strength equal to ten elephants and rejoices together with the gods.
Having taken the three fruits (*triphalā*) there, one should cast them into the mountain water; when that [mixture] has become solid as stone, one should take it and grind it into powder.

One should consume that mercury, once it has been well-digested, together with ghee and honey, for one year; thereafter, one should subsist on milk alone. Then, resembling the rising sun, one becomes intelligent and pleasing to behold.
And one with dark, curly hair shall live as long as the moon, sun, and stars. One should combine together mercury,
yellow orpiment, realgar, pyrite,
cinnabar, and poison.
One should grind it on a grinding stone; having formed a ball with the juice of *mātuluṅga*, one should place it in the midst of water. By that means, silver and copper certainly become gold.

One should consume it for one month; he will be free from wrinkles and grey hair, and his lifespan will be a thousand years, endowed with great strength and prowess. By merely adding a sprinkling of its powder to turmeric that has been turned into stone, [the same result is achieved].
The nāga attains the state of blood, possessing a radiance like that of the rising sun.
Having cast it into mountain water, or into earth, rock, or even mud,
one should bind the mercury after determining the duration of time.

Blown together with red alkali, gold that has been amalgamated with all metals by a hundredth part acts as a transmuter of gold. Having obtained a second amalgamation, one should consume it with honey and clarified butter.
At that time, for those [impurities] born of the mind, the wind arises above.
He will possess knowledge of the time; he shall live for fifty thousand years. Having attained the second extraction (*sāraṇā*), he pierces with a thousandth part.
One should hold that pill in the mouth; one certainly attains divinity.
[It may be made] from *nicula*, *kakubha*, *kiṃśuka*, or *madhuka*, or from the interior of the fruit of *iṅgudī*, or from the midst of the two types of *rajanī*.
One should grind mercury and sulphur into the form of pills and cook them for one day; then, having encased them in gold,
one should wear them, carefully wrapping them with a paste of *triphalā* and *vyoṣa*.
Having added a quarter-part of gold, one should join mercury to it and cast it into the midst of mountain-water;
the pill will become like a diamond.
As before, the process of *sāraṇā* should be performed; as before, it shall bestow success.

When held in the mouth, it indeed bestows a lifespan of a thousand years. Through the application of the second *sāraṇā*, when held in the mouth, it pierces ten thousand; this very [practice] becomes the giver of a lifespan of ten thousand years.
Through the third process of refinement (*sāraṇā*), it becomes capable of piercing a *lakṣa*;
one should wear that *khoṭa* in the mouth, and the man attains a lifespan of a *lakṣa*.
Having attained the fourth refinement, there is no doubt that it pierces a *koṭi*.
His lifespan shall be ten million years, and he attains the power of moving through the sky.
With five [repetitions], there shall be one hundred million; with six, there shall be one billion, until his life lasts as long as the sun and moon, possessing infinite strength and vigor.

She also bestows the seventh [siddhi]. That supreme pill is known as Sāraṇā, renowned by the name Khecarī, and was impelled by Bhairava. He who should consume even a mere grain of mustard seed of it for one month—
He becomes a perfected one (*siddha*) with a vajra-body; beloved by divine women, he sports with the enjoyments of the sky-goers (*khecara*). By his own will, he attains the state of Śiva.
There shall also be various kinds of fruits, [obtained] from their juices and from seed-oils.
That mercury is indeed bound; listen, O beautiful one, to [the method for] the pill.
When the pure, bound mercury has been digested with three times its weight of sulphur, one should then produce gold with that [mixture].

One should cause the mercury to be reduced to ash; therein, the gold is the mercury, and that ash is to be digested within the mercury, equal to the mercury itself. By means of that mercury which has been fully digested, one should digest the diamond-gem.

That vajra is reduced to ash, resembling the crimson hue of vermilion. That ash digests mercury; when the three qualities have been honored with wine, one should extract that [mercury] into gold and fashion a pill from it.

Having placed that [substance], encased in the three metals, into his mouth, the practitioner becomes one whose shadow has vanished; he becomes invisible even to gods and dānavas. O Goddess, at that very moment, it transforms all metals into gold.

For many thousands of years, one shall be free from wrinkles and gray hair. One should hold in one's mouth and hand the Trident-bearer (Śūlin) joined with the Spear (Śakti), adorned with the qualities of jewels and so forth; for this wards off all weapons.
Space, the essence of *mākṣika*, pure silver (*tārāmātra*), the weapon of the gods (*surāyudha*),
*vaikrānta*, *tālaka*, and mercury— adorned with the qualities of gems and other substances,
this pill, O beautiful lady, is joined with the three sweets (*madhuratraya*).
Situated in the mouth, it shall directly destroy graying hair; of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess of gods, Śiva and Śakti are like gems and so forth residing within Śiva. One should cause gold, silver, and copper to be made in equal proportions.
One should wrap female menstrual blood placed in the midst of tiger-skin with a lotus fiber.
Having thus wrapped it, one should sprinkle it and deposit it in a secret place. In battle, in the royal court, in gambling, in divine rites, or in matters of desire, victory shall be attained.

And that globule which is placed in the mouth— he shall become a delighter of all. Vaikrānta, abhraka, kānta, sasyaka, and surāyudha should be equal in measure to the kāñcika produced from vibhītaka and other such sources.

Then one produces *rājāvarta*; having ground it with the juice of *kumārī*, one should join it by means of a foot-measure. A single auspicious pill thus prepared destroys disease, death, and old age; when held in the mouth, there is no doubt of this.

O lady of excellent hips! [The mixture consists of] five stars, two births, and three parts of the sky; each one [part] belongs to gold and mercury. By means of the half-copper preparation, O beautiful lady of the immortal, [one obtains] the pill.

For by this one becomes inexhaustible and indeed ageless, possessed of great strength, and liberated from all diseases; one shall live [long] by holding it in the mouth. Likewise, one *pala* of ash-mercury (*bhasmasūta*) and one *pala* of dead iron (*mṛtakānta*).
One *pala* of honey, one *pala* of *śilājatu*,
one *pala* of *viḍaṅga*, and likewise one *pala* of powdered *pathyā*;
having combined all of this, one should grind it with honey and clarified butter.
O Goddess, one should have three hundred and sixty pills prepared;
one should consume them daily, continuously for one year. One shall live for thousands of years, possessing great strength equal to Rudra.
Henceforth I shall proclaim the elixir of mercury-ash (*rasabhasmarasāyana*), which is to be known as free from restrictions and is a supreme, manifest divine medicine.
[It consists of] *āmalaka* and other such [herbs], *kānta* iron, mercury, and realgar (*manaḥśilā*).

And one should add one-seventh part of *vākucī*. Ground with the juice of *kṣīriṇī* and combined with the juice of *meghanāda*, it should be placed in a "mute" crucible (*mūkamūṣā*) and subjected to heating (*puṭa*).
One should consume it in sequence, starting with one *māṣa*, then three *māṣas*, and then triple that amount.
O Goddess, after three years, he shall gradually receive half a *niṣka* per day;
for six, seven, and eight years, respectively, according to the measure of *niṣkas*,
he shall enjoy divine food, free from old age and deformity.
Whoever consumes for three years a small amount combined with gold—whether a *niṣka* or even half a *niṣka*—will thoroughly conquer all diseases.
At eight years [of practice], one has a lifespan of a thousand years; at twelve years, one is capable of piercing a target from a distance of a hundred thousand leagues.

O Goddess, in the sixteenth year, he becomes possessed of a divine form. (RA 12.363) One hundred *pala* of *abhayā*, as well as *akṣa* and *dhātrī*, are boiled in eight hundred parts of water until one-eighth remains. This decoction is enriched with ghee, honey, and sugar, and mixed with a tenth part of the three pungents (*vyoṣa*) and *citraka*. It is then processed with the juice of meat and fruit, and combined with iron that has been both digested and calcined. (Ras 12.364)
Viḍaṅga, which resembles mountain-ash (giri-jatu) and possesses lovely black bees [upon it], should be well-matured with mercury and the finest divine rice.

This paste, prepared from *ahimara* and kept in an iron vessel for three days until it is thoroughly processed, is most excellent. One who consumes this at bedtime, while attending to his beautiful-eyed beloved, becomes possessed of a firm and compact waist and gains the pride of an elephant in rut. *Rasārṇava 12.365*

Free from every fault, possessing divine vision in all directions, he was as lovely as the God of Love to women—a preeminent hero. (Ras 12.366) With a body like a fresh rain-cloud and hair as dark as curled locks, he was as pure as the Preceptor of the Gods; a true poet and a creator of wonders, his gait and movements were like those of a bull, and his voice was smooth and deep. Like the celestial elephant in this world, he was a constant destroyer of fatigue. (Ras 12.367)
Indeed, he who lives by the moon, stars, and sun; who possesses the great beauty of the lotus-dwelling goddess; who is a knower of the treatises on logic and other sciences;

who is a protector of the conventions of the virtuous and a follower of the initiation into Dharma; who is as profound as Hari, Hara, and Maheśvara; and who is as steadfast as the sun, the moon, and the ocean—by him, mercury, gold, copper, iron, mica, and *golaka* are placed within the fruit of the *iṅgudī*. (Rasāyana 12.368)
The *golaka* of stone, water, mercury, and *siddha*— beautiful, auspicious, and pleasing to the immortals;
*kānta*, gold, the sun, the moon, mica, the diamond-gem,
and the *golaka* of the king of serpents— when these are cast into the hollow of an *āmalaka* wood and buried in the earth or a mountain, they are extracted [as elixirs].
Then, having placed the enemy who has become like a mountain into the mouth, one attains a vajra-body in a few days.
With *tāla*, excellent gold, copper, and mercury, a ball (*golaka*) is fashioned, secured by a wooden frame and the beautiful essence of *śailavāri*; this is called the *khecarī* pill.
One should eat the palāśa seed cast into mountain water, processed with honey and ghee, for twenty-one days, taking it once every day; such a man shall live for a thousand years and be victorious.
Likewise, one may take mercury and mica combined with the milk of the *vajrī* plant.
Combined with gold, it becomes the Khecarī pill.
One should place mercury within the fruit of the Karañja tree; situated in the midst of ghee, rock-salt, and water, it bestows a lifespan of a thousand years.
In *tinduka* one has a lifespan of two thousand; in *jambīra*, three thousand;
and in *mātuluṅga* and *nāraṅga*, four and five thousand respectively.
In the fruit of *rambhā* it is six thousand, and in *panasa* it is seven thousand.
In the *vibhītaka* fruit, it is ten thousand in number.
In the coconut, O highly fortunate one, it is fourteen thousand;
in the lotus, thirty thousand; and in the *āmalaka*, furthermore, it is one hundred thousand.

A decoction [is prepared] in the liquid of mica-leaf; from that, mercury extracted in *śilodaka* for a day and night destroys death and poverty. Through the application of the process of *sāraṇā*, a new body is born.

In alchemy (*rasāyana*) and in the extraction of essences (*rasa*), one becomes a piercer of a hundred thousand targets; of this there is no doubt. By heating a ball (*golakam*) made from the essence of *kardama* and *kumārī*, the vital essence (*sattva*) falls out; a person should hold that in their mouth.

By practicing this for six months, one indeed attains freedom from old age and death. When *srotoñjana* is heated together with mercury (*pārada*) mixed with *sattva*, one should hold that pill (*khoṭa*) in the mouth; one certainly becomes invisible.

Whichever procedure has been prescribed for whom— whether it be water or indeed mercury at the proper time according to the Śivāgama— one should certainly perform that elixir (*rasāyana*). (RA 12.382) 13
The Goddess said:
O Lord, you have explained to me the digestion (*jāraṇā*) of mercury (*pārada*) by means of a "child" (*bāla*).
Hereafter, please explain correctly the digestion of that which has been properly bound (*samyagbaddha*).
The illustrious Bhairava said: (2.1) That which was previously described is this inferior *bālajāraṇā* (the digestion of the raw).
(2.2) Now hear of the superior and rare *baddhajāraṇā* (the digestion of the bound). (RA_13.2.3)
He who swallows mercury that is unbonded will himself go to destruction as it is digested;
but for one who has bonded it, the morsel is digested, and once digested, the mouth [of the practitioner] becomes open.
One with a beautiful face, free from defects, possesses the complete and supreme marks.
Ordinary [mercury] is characterized by its resistance to fire; it is the "digestive" agent for great jewels.
First, the ordinary mercury should be prepared; indeed, that which possesses the capacity for "devouring" is highly esteemed.
